items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: That was a big experience with Benny Carter, John Collins, Kenny Clark and Sonny White.

ctx.x: And didn't he subsequently work with you?

Well, he made records with me and we worked together in 1942 with Benny Carter and that was a great experience too because we had two -- three of the foremost exponents of the instrument like -- three. There was Benny Carter, there was Kenny Clark, there was John and then there was Sonny White, and that was a great experience for me too because well at that time I was getting a little name and I was getting a new dialogue, you know, setting up notes together. That was a big experience with Benny Carter, John…

band too.
John was really one of the major voices on the guitar. Before Charley Christian came, John was the guitar player, the guitar player, you know. Of course when Charley Christian came on the scene, Charley Christian had a far western outlook to music, you know, like Oklahoma. So he had that thing and that really set his apart from the rest of the musicians and then he came into jamming with us. So John was really a major voice.
